thread:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: GPU ECC/Xid anomaly detected — spike in Xid 13/32 driver resets across rack gpu-pool-3. Rate: 5 resets/min over last 6m. Auto-escalation -> #incidents paging.

alex (oncall): seeing elevated 502s from inference-service on node gpu-03 and gpu-07. Confirming container restarts. paging now.

maya (eng-sre): thanks — I'm pulling node metrics. Can you paste the top container logs from gpu-03? suspecting OOM before driver reset.

jamal (eng-runtime): sharing kernel dmesg from gpu-03, truncated:```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (0001:02) 13 at 0xabcdef: GPU has fallen off the bus.
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: Xid (0001:02) 32 at 0xabcdf0: a GPU memory ECC error was detected.
[ 12345.680000] docker: containerd: runtime: process killed due to signal 6
```

priya (support): customers flagged: search-api-prod (4% error increase), chat-saas (timeouts), one internal canary. CS bridge queued for 10m. erin, can you confirm which tenants are impacted?

erin (cs): confirmed - search-api-prod and chat-saas showing increased latency. No billing impact reported yet. I've opened a bridge with customer success for chat-saas. briar joining.

briar (customer-suc): on bridge — relaying that customer saw 10% request failures starting 3:08pm UTC. They want ETA.

maya (eng-sre): quick triage: telemetry shows ECC error rate correlated with nodes on a specific kernel + nvidia driver bundle (510.85.x) — looks like recent rolling driver update 12h ago touched these hosts.

alex (oncall): status update to channel: cordoning and draining gpu-03 and gpu-07 now, redirecting traffic to warm pool. Starting graceful evict with 5m grace.

ops-bot: Command executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-03 && kubectl drain gpu-03 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=300`

jamal (eng-runtime): mitigation plan: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes (done by alex) 2) roll back driver to previous stable 470.xx on a canary node 3) enable persistent process restart (systemd) and disable CUDA persistence mode toggles 4) enable fallback model variant for latency-sensitive routes to avoid GPU-heavy paths.

maya (eng-sre): I'll run `nvml-scan --history 24h --filter Xid` to enumerate other suspects. If we see >3 nodes with same signature, we escalate to infra for BMC-level checks.

alex (oncall): drained gpu-03, draining gpu-07 now. Redirecting load. Observed immediate drop in errors for requests hitting warm pool.

priya (support): updating customers: "We're mitigating a GPU driver issue causing intermittent inference failures. Our engineers are draining affected hosts and applying a rollback on a canary node. We'll update in 15m."

jamal (eng-runtime): rolling driver rollback to 470.105.03 on node gpu-canary-1 now. Command: ```ansible -i hosts[gpu-canary-1] playbooks/driver-rollback.yml -e driver_version=470.105.03```

ops-bot: playbook started; ETA ~8m.

maya (eng-sre): note: there's a hardware ECC sensor alert on gpu-07 (board temp spike before Xid). Recommend we cordon gpu-07 permanently pending hardware inspection. Marking gpu-07 as quarantined.

alex (oncall): acknowledged. Marking gpu-07 out-of-service.

jamal (eng-runtime): canary finished rollback — driver back to 470 and persistence process restarted. Running stress test overlay and sending a small traffic surge to canary variant. Logs so far: no Xids in the 10m after rollback.

maya (eng-sre): scanning fleet: 2 additional nodes show historical matches but low frequency. I'll schedule immediate rolling audit of nodes that received the 510.85 bundle.

erin (cs): customers updated. chat-saas bridge: they accept mitigation; want postmortem when stable.

briar (customer-suc): noted, asking for timeline for hardware check on gpu-07.

alex (oncall): next steps: keep drained nodes offline, complete driver rollback across nodes that got 510.85 in the last 24h but only after canary validation. Escalate hardware team for gpu-07. Priya/Erin to manage customer comms. Jamal and Maya continue telemetry and rollback.

priya (support): tagging next oncall for handoff in 45m: @sam (oncall-next). Will prepare handoff notes including affected nodes, driver versions, customers impacted, and actions taken.

jamal (eng-runtime): temp workaround added to runtime: if Xid sequence detected >2 in 60s, runtime auto-falls back to CPU-based model variant and returns 503 to indicate graceful degradation to caller with a header `x-rw-fallback: true`. Patch:```diff
- if (xid_count > 2) crash();
+ if (xid_count > 2) fallback_to_cpu(); // avoid node reboot cascade
```

maya (eng-sre): logs show error budget impact ~0.6% for search-api-prod since spike. We'll include SLO delta in postmortem.

ops-bot: Incident severity updated to SEV2 by alex — potential customer impact but mitigated.

alex (oncall): handing off to sam in 40m. Handoff note: cause: driver+kernel combo appears to surface ECC/Xid leading to driver resets; mitigation: drain/quarantine, driver rollback, runtime fallback. Action items: continue fleet scan, hardware check for gpu-07, and coordinate postmortem.

sam (oncall-next): acked — will take over in 40m. Please drop me a short runbook pointer and the `nvml-scan` output when ready.

maya (eng-sre): dropping runbook link and nvml summary in thread: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/gpu-xid-handoff (pasted for sam). nvml-summary: nodes with 510.85: gpu-03, gpu-07 (quarantined), gpu-12 (low), gpu-19 (low).

priya (support): final note: customer impact tracked, CS will request a scheduled maintenance window for gpu-07 repair. I'll open a ticket with infra.

IncidentBot: Incident closed to paging; follow-ups in thread.

alex (oncall): thanks team. Will start the postmortem draft once we have full nvml logs and driver rollout timeline.

sam (oncall-next): thanks — taking it from here.
